questions.q: AFC stands for:
questions.explain: Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) is the gate-and-card system that lets passengers in and collects the fare without a ticket window.

questions.q: The main components of an Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system are:
options: Gates, ticket vending machines, card readers and a central clearing system
questions.explain: Gates (flap barriers), Ticket Vending Machines (TVMs), readers and the central clearing house make up Automatic Fare Collection (AFC).

questions.q: TVM stands for:
questions.explain: Ticket Vending Machines (TVMs) are the self-service machines that sell/issue tickets and cards.

questions.q: NCMC stands for:
questions.explain: National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) — 'One Nation One Card' — is designed to work across metros, Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) and buses like one ATM card in every bank.

questions.q: Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) supports which fare media?
options: National Common Mobility Card (NCMC), Quick Response (QR) tickets and contactless payment
questions.explain: Namo Bharat ticketing works with National Common Mobility Card (NCMC), Quick Response (QR) and digital/contactless payment.

questions.q: The 'central clearing' function in Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) does the job of:
options: Settling and reconciling fare transactions centrally across the system
questions.explain: Clearing is the back-office settlement that sorts out who gets what from each card journey.

questions.q: Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) gates at stations are usually of which type?
questions.explain: Flap-barrier gates open on a valid tap and close behind the passenger.

questions.q: Besides collecting fares, Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) data helps operations by:
questions.explain: Gate data shows where and when crowds build — operations uses it to plan service and staffing.

questions.q: PIS stands for:
questions.explain: Passenger Information System (PIS) is the displays/boards side of passenger information.

questions.q: PAS stands for:
questions.explain: Public Address System (PAS) is the announcement side — spoken information to passengers.

questions.q: Passenger Information Display System (PIDS) displays at stations show:
options: Train timings, destinations and disruption information
questions.explain: Passenger Information Displays carry timings, destinations, delays and safety messages.

questions.q: Help points/intercoms at stations are part of:
options: Passenger information/communication systems — the Passenger Information System (PIS) family
Traction Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA)
questions.explain: Help points connect passengers to staff — they sit with the Passenger Information System (PIS)/communication family.

questions.q: During an incident, passenger information given out must be:
options: Approved and accurate information from Operations Control Centre (OCC), to prevent panic and rumours
questions.explain: In incidents, accurate Operations Control Centre (OCC)-approved information is an operational duty — wrong information creates panic.

questions.q: Why is accurate passenger information called an operational duty, not a courtesy?
options: Because wrong or absent information causes panic, rumours and unsafe crowd behaviour
questions.explain: Crowds act on information; controlling information is part of controlling the incident.

questions.q: A smart card tap at the gate is an example of:
options: Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) in action — the same card family works across systems
questions.explain: Your metro/National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) card tapping at the gate is Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) — one card, many systems.

questions.q: If Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) gates at a station fail during peak hour, operations must:
options: Manage passenger entry/exit by the prescribed fallback (staff-supervised/manual arrangements) and report the fault
questions.explain: Fare system failure is handled by controlled manual fallback and fault reporting — passengers still travel safely.

questions.q: Quick Response (QR) tickets in Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) are used as:
options: A fare medium validated at Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) gates
A type of Platform Screen Door (PSD)
questions.explain: Quick Response (QR)-based tickets are scanned at the gates just like cards are tapped.

questions.q: Station computer in the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) chain does what?
options: Drives the trains at that station
Collects and manages the station's AFC data and links it to the central system
questions.explain: Each station's Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) equipment reports through its station computer to the central clearing system.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) component?
questions.explain: Eurobalises belong to European Train Control System (ETCS) signalling; the rest are Automatic Fare Collection (AFC).

questions.q: Passenger load patterns from Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) data would most help Operations Control Centre (OCC) decide:
options: Where crowding is building and whether service/staffing needs adjustment
questions.explain: Entry/exit counts by station and time are a live crowding picture for controllers.

questions.q: During a service disruption, Passenger Information System (PIS)/Public Address System (PAS) should announce:
options: The disruption, its effect and what passengers should do — accurately and promptly
questions.explain: Disruption information is safety information: what happened, what it means, what to do.

questions.q: A display shows a wrong destination for a departing train. This is:
options: An operational fault to be corrected immediately, because passengers act on it
questions.explain: Wrong information moves crowds wrongly — treat it as a real fault and fix/announce the correction.

questions.q: Contactless payment at gates means:
options: Passengers can pay/enter using contactless cards or devices without a separate ticket purchase step
questions.explain: Contactless media speed up entry — the fare is still collected by Automatic Fare Collection (AFC).

questions.q: The link between Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) and operations is that:
options: AFC is both the fare system and a source of passenger-flow intelligence for operations
questions.explain: Gates collect money and data; operations uses the data.

questions.q: If a passenger's card is rejected at the gate, the front-line resolution point is:
options: The Operations Control Centre (OCC) chief controller personally
Station staff/customer care handling as per Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) procedure, not the train operator
questions.explain: Card/gate issues are station-level Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) matters handled by station staff.

questions.q: Why do Passenger Information System (PIS) announcements during incidents come from/through Operations Control Centre (OCC) approval?
options: To keep one consistent, verified version of information across all stations and trains
questions.explain: One source = one story; conflicting local guesses create rumours and panic.

questions.q: Tokens, in systems that use them, are:
options: A single-journey fare medium handled by the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system
questions.explain: Do not confuse Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) journey tokens with block-working tokens — context decides the meaning.

questions.q: A station's Public Address (PA) announcement cannot be heard on the platform. Operationally this is:
options: A Public Address System (PAS) fault to report — in an emergency that platform cannot receive spoken instructions
questions.explain: If people cannot hear announcements, emergency communication to that platform is broken — report it.

questions.q: The Passenger Information System (PIS) inside the train and the PIS at the station should:
options: Tell a consistent story, both fed from the same operational information
questions.explain: Consistency between on-train and station information keeps passengers calm and correctly directed.

questions.q: The one-line summary of Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) + Passenger Information System (PIS) for operations is:
options: AFC and PIS are purely commercial systems
AFC moves passengers in and counts them; PIS/Public Address System (PAS) keeps them informed — both are operational tools, not just passenger conveniences
questions.explain: Fare collection, crowd data and passenger information all feed directly into running the railway.

questions.q: In a closed Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system, a passenger who taps in at entry but does not tap out at exit will generally face:
options: An incomplete journey — the system cannot calculate the fare, so the card is charged as per rule (often the maximum fare) or has to be regularised at the station
questions.explain: Fare is calculated from the entry–exit pair. A missing exit tap leaves an incomplete journey in the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system, settled by the railway's rule, not by guesswork at the gate.

questions.q: Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) gate lanes at a station can be set as entry-only, exit-only or bi-directional. Operations changes these modes mainly to:
options: Match the direction of the passenger rush — more entry lanes in the morning peak, more exit lanes in the evening peak
Reduce the number of staff on duty
questions.explain: Peak flow is one-directional. Reversible Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) lanes let the station pour its gate capacity into the direction passengers are actually moving.

questions.q: A passenger reports a lost smart card and it is 'blacklisted' in the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system. This means:
options: Only the reporting station will reject it
The card number is blocked centrally, so gates across the network will reject it if anyone tries to use it
The card is physically destroyed at the station counter
The passenger can never travel again
questions.explain: Blacklisting works because Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) is networked: one report at any station protects the balance at every gate on the system.

questions.q: On the Passenger Information System (PIS) and Public Address System (PAS), message priority during operations is:
options: Commercial advertisements first, train information later
Safety and emergency messages override everything else; routine service information comes next
questions.explain: Passenger Information System (PIS) displays and Public Address System (PAS) announcements follow a priority ladder — an emergency instruction must never wait behind a routine or commercial message.

questions.q: If the central Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) system or its link to a station fails, well-designed station gates keep working by:
options: Refusing every passenger until the link returns
Working in offline mode — validating cards locally and storing the transactions to upload when the link is restored
questions.explain: Offline working is graceful degradation for Automatic Fare Collection (AFC): passengers keep moving, transactions are stored at the station, and the central system settles them later.
